A delegation of the ICRC was prohibited again yesterday from visiting Bratunac, the town in Srebrenica where many of the captured men are believed to be held." So that's the 17th of July. The media in London is already reporting concerns that many captured Muslim men aren't being allowed to be visited by the ICRC. Then if we go to another article, P4398. This is now the 21st of July. And again it's "The Independent" in London, and the report starts off: "Just across the Drina River from the sleepy Serbian town of Ljubovija a slaughter is said to be taking place, possibly the biggest mass execution of Muslim prisoners by the Bosnian Serbs in more than three years." So that's what the media in London knows. The specific reference to Muslim prisoners of war isn't it? And yet you testify that it was never emphasised that these were prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking about our media, not "The Independent" and other foreign media.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Right. So the international media in London, by the 21st of July, was reporting about the possible biggest mass execution of Muslim prisoners in the whole war, and the local media knew nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a time of relentless propaganda so it is very hard to believe everything that was written. If such a report was accurate it was shocking, but you know that the media liked to add ingredients to their stories, and if you repeat one thing on a daily basis, one starts to believe that. I was an ordinary citizen, and I followed that as an ordinary citizen, and unfortunately I knew nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: General, when at any other point in the war did you ever hear a rumour or propaganda about 4.000 prisoners of war being executed? When did you ever hear that at any other point in the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You're not -- you're an expert witness, General. You're not seriously suggesting that the international media in London knows more about what was happening in Eastern Bosnia than the president of the republic who sat at the top of the army, the police, and the civilian authorities who were working hand-in-hand to execute and bury these prisoners? That's not your expert testimony, is it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just tell you how the president of the republic, i.e., the Supreme Commander, executed his command role. That was done by personal --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- insight or through information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: General, let me stop you there. I don't want a long explanation of his command role. I'm just asking are you seriously suggesting that the international media knew more about what was going on in Eastern Bosnia than the president of the republic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, your people were filming that, and they knew better the situation, and they were able to know at every point in time what exactly was happening. The question is why didn't they prevent it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Well, I think when you say "your people were filming that," it was Zoran Petrovic, a Serb journalist, embedded in a Serb MUP unit who filmed that, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was filming the taking of prisoners, not the killings. He was travel around the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road and was filming the surrender of the people in the column, as far as I can remember the footage. He might have some other footage of which I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You're aware of the footage of the Kravica warehouse on the afternoon of 13 July, aren't you, the bodies piled up in front of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And that was taken by Zoran Petrovic, a Serb cameraman embedded in a Bosnian Serb MUP unit.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. As for the filming in the area of Zvornik Brigade, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: One -- one final area, General. Paragraph 427 of your report. This is Exhibit D3864. It's 161 in the English and 186 in the B/C/S. You'll see in this paragraph, General, you say that Mr. Karadzic did not know that there was no fighting against the Muslim forces in the Pilica area. And this is in the context of his report on the 23rd of March, 1996. So let me turn that around. If he doesn't know that there was no fighting, he doesn't know that there was fighting either; right? He doesn't know either way.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He knew that there were activities in the general area, but he didn't know specifically about Pilica. He couldn't have known that, because there were actually no operations there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That's my point. He didn't know that there was any fighting there; right? Specifically in Pilica, he didn't know that there was any fighting?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He thought that there was fighting, but by way of his order he just demonstrated that he actually didn't know. That was a locality in the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade, and therefore he was supposed to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: General, let's get this very clear. You say he did not know that there was no fighting in your report. So --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: He doesn't know for sure that there was fighting, did he? He just doesn't know either way.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But one can deduce from the order that he thought that there was fighting. If you look at this document, it seems that he believed there were operations there. The best way would possibly be to look at the document so that we can confirm that he was convinced that there was fighting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let me show you another document. This is Exhibit P1490. If we can have page 47 in the English and 44 in the B/C/S. General, what you're going to see here are General Mladic's notes of a conversation that he had with President Karadzic on the 22nd of March. So that's the day before President Karadzic issued this order to investigate armed conflict in Pilica. You can see at the top point President Karadzic is recorded as saying: A big show was put on for Albright. She expected they would find 1.200 Muslim bodies at Pilica but they found some five bodies. And then the third bullet point down says: Fico was here last night and he says those two will sell their story about Srebrenica to The Hague. General, you know who Drazen Erdemovic is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And you know that Drazen Erdemovic was addressed in March 1996 in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And he was arrested with one other person, Radislav Kremenovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let me show you 65 ter 25423. What you're going to see, General, is an article published by "Slobodna Bosna" on the 22nd of March, 1996. So this is the same day as President Karadzic's meeting with General Mladic and the day before the order to investigate armed conflict in Pilica. What you're seeing here is an interview with Drazen Erdemovic. If we go over to the next page in English, we'll see at the very top Erdemovic -- Erdemovic, a story about killing 1.200 Muslim civilians at Pilica in July 1995 at a farm in Pilica. So 22nd of March, 1996, Erdemovic's story gets published in your local press; right? This is not international media. This is Serb press.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a reference confirming that "Slobodna Bosna" is a Serb media outlet? Where was it published at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, that's not a proper intervention. You can ask it in your re-examination, Mr. Karadzic. Shall we continue. You're coming to a close.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Very close, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: General, you'd agree that Drazen Erdemovic's interview on the 22nd of March where he says -- or talks about killing 1.200 Muslim civilians at Pilica is quite clearly what President Karadzic and General Mladic were talking about in their meeting where President Karadzic said Albright expected they would find 1.200 Muslim bodies at Pilica. They're obviously talking about the same thing; right? The story that Erdemovic had told about the 1.200 Muslims being killed.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer from the beginning. We couldn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Karadzic is saying this indeed, but he was considered this to be a propaganda stunt and that that number of dead bodies would not be found, hence he ordered a commission to be formed, made up of representatives of the MUP, the Main Staff, and the IFOR. And he wanted to once and for all suppress Albright's propaganda about the massacres and dead bodies. Do you really think that he would go as far to establish a commission if he knew that that would be established as a fact on the spot? I really cannot suppose and even think possible if Karadzic would act with such a high degree of hypocrisy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Well, General, we've seen evidence in this case - this is Exhibit 4487 - that the 10th Sabotage Detachment, which Drazen Erdemovic was a member of, was the VRS's first professional unit. Erdemovic was a professional VRS soldier. His contract, which is in evidence here was personally signed by General Mladic, and he was given an exceptional promotion after the Srebrenica operation. So here is a decorated professional VRS soldier making a public statement about having participated in the execution of 1.200 Muslim civilians. And despite having this information on the 22nd of March, the next day President Karadzic issues an order specifically saying investigate armed conflict in the Pilica area. Now, this is quite clearly a deliberate attempt to cover up the killings in Pilica, isn't it? He's trying to get a cover story out there that we all have to say this is armed conflict. That's what the 23 March order is; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary. On the contrary. He's issuing an order to investigate the allegations and to determine whether really dead bodies came to the surface or whether it was propaganda. Based on that, I concluded that he didn't know about it. If he knew about it, he wouldn't bring in IFOR and the MUP and Main Staff. He wouldn't have set up the commission and expect the commission to produce findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And in that order, if you look back at your report which you quote there, President Karadzic says: Follow the same procedure in other similar cases. This was at paragraph 425 of your report, General.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You see that there where President Karadzic says follow the same procedure in other similar cases. The only other cases remotely similar to Pilica were Kravica, Orahovac, Petkovci, and Kozluk; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that this refers to this case. If we are talking about investigations and setting up commissions, then the presumption is that commissions had been formed in the preceding period and that they were expected to operate in the same manner. This is how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Last question, General. You agreed earlier today at page 18 that President Karadzic in his capacity of Supreme Commander had to authorise the taking of Srebrenica because it was a substantive change --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are overhearing something. Mr. Mitchell, could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You agreed earlier today that President Karadzic in his capacity of Supreme Commander had to authorise the taking of Srebrenica because it was a substantive change in the objective of Krivaja 95. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Just answer yes or no to the next question if you can: The decision to execute thousands of Muslim prisoners captured after the fall of Srebrenica, that's also a substantive change in the objective of the Krivaja 95 operation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I can't give you a yes or no answer to this question. It's so leading that I cannot give you the answer as you wish. It's not one and the same thing to approve the expansion of an operational plan on the grounds of professional and military reasons to take control of certain area as opposed to an order to execute prisoners. The former order exists, and the latter does not exist. Therefore, I cannot give you such a simple answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us please pause between questions and answers. We need to be mindful of that. General, let us start with the most recent question put to you about the fate of the POWs following the fall of Srebrenica. Did you know and did you establish within whose scope of responsibility and at what level the care and exchange of prisoners existed on the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the exchange of prisoners on the Serbian side was executed from the grass root levels to the very top leadership of the army.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have 1D25242.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we don't have a translation yet, but I would kindly ask you to briefly read a portion and tell us what this document represents.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this please be zoomed in. Command of the Drina Corps, 10th July 1995, Government of Republika Srpska, State Commission for exchange of prisoners of war, reference to a certain document, and then the text: "Due to active combat operations carried out by the enemy on all front lines in the area of responsibility of the Sarajevo Romanija and Drina Corps and since the Muslim offensive is still ongoing we believe that negotiations about the exchange of POWs with the Muslim side should be conducted after the cessation of hostile activities. Due to that, the representatives of the commission for the exchange of the Drina Corps shall not attend the meeting convened for 11th of July in Kiseljak," signed Milenko Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, what do you think about the possibility of an exchange of prisoners in the middle of an offensive?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not possible. It's impossible to achieve due to security reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this please be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3865, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 1D25243.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately this has not yet been translated.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's a new document. Can you identify it, who is the author, and the date?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Drina Corps, exchange of POW --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please read a little bit more slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Radinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you start over again and read very slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's done, General, I think. Now the text.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Since the establishment of contact and the conduct of negotiations on exchanges of prisoners of war is under the commission for exchanges of POWs of the Drina Corps, we agree with the position that you presented in your document. "Therefore, if there is a call and if the Muslim side insists via radio communications to establish contact regarding exchanges of prisoners of war, communicate to them that they can -- that a contact can be agreed only between the president of the commission of the district of Tuzla and the president of the commission of the Drina Corps. "The commission for the exchange of POWs with the Drina Corps shall agree on a meeting with the Muslim side in order to negotiate on the exchange with the agreement of the Main Staff of the VRS until a favourable situation occurs and information is -- and information that is indispensable for talks is accumulated."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: That is the end of the text. We did not hear what the General after that. It was too fast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat who signed this, because the interpreters didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Major-General Radislav Krstic, but someone signed for him, for him. Somebody was probably authorised to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything unusual in this text that would indicate that this text was taking place during exchanges -- or talks on exchanges?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing unnatural here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was not interpreted beforehand who this was sent to.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander is sending this to the 1st Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: No objection to it being marked for identification, but perhaps the General's attention could be drawn to the date of the document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I didn't follow you, Mr. Mitchell. Mr. Karadzic referred to the date, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If he did, then I'll withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably that maybe I read that myself. Thank you. Shall we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the Drina Corps in charge of exchanging prisoners that they had taken prisoner themselves? Is this something that comes out of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Drina Corps is authorised for the exchange of prisoners of war for as long as they are in its area of responsibility. At the moment when the POWs go to Batkovici, then the exchange of POWs is raised to a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have this document admitted for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: First shall we assign a number for the previous document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D25243 will be MFI D3866.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have two admitted ones; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second now. But, General, this was dated 21st of July. You agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said that in my answer. The last sentence had to do with the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3866, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D25244. Could we please take a look at that now. I believe that there is a translation, so could we have both versions. Yes, we have the Serb version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the English one could you please take a look at who is writing this and to whom.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the State Commission for the exchange of prisoners of war of the Government of Republika Srpska that is writing this document. And they're writing to commissions to the exchange of prisoners of war of various corps. They are receiving this information, commission for the exchange of POWs of the 1st Corps, the 2nd Corps, the IBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, you don't have to read out all of this. Could we have this just by way of a summary. What are they looking for?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The subject is gathering information. Considering the current situation concerning the -- is this Croatia aggression against the area of the Republic of Serb Krajina? It will be necessary to participate actively in the forthcoming period and gathering information about missing, dead, and captured soldiers and civilians from the area of the Republic of Serb Krajina in addition to our regular activities and task. Our next activities will also be directed at solving problems that have occurred within our domain and that relate to the area of the Republic of the Serb Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, no. When reading, could you read slow and speak into the microphone for the benefit of the interpreters. And, Mr. Karadzic, repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, could you just interpret this for us, this last paragraph. What does it say there? This action in your view, is this customary? Is this a routine matter in the process?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is necessary to submit information to the State Commission for the exchange of prisoners of war. Yes, this is quite customary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we see the date here, the 10th of August on the stamp?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th of August at 11.50. I assume it is 1995, but the date cannot really be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the heading we see 95 within the number, and on the stamp we see August.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And signed State Commission for the exchange of prisoners of war, Bulajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, is this customary that the Drina Corps -- or rather, corps as such communicate with the State Commission? Or rather, did you find any document, any example of these corps commissions for exchanges address me?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not come across a document in which they were addressing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3867, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D25245. Could we please have that document now? There is a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, could you please read this to yourself, page 1, so that you familiarise yourself with it, and then I'm going to put a question to you. General, sir, can you tell us -- I think we need the next page in English. The second paragraph. The Serb commission proposes that the issue be resolved on the principle of one for one.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is the extent of the knowledge of the commission for the exchange of prisoners since they suggest that this principle of one for one should be applied to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose the commission presumes that there were prisoners taken on all sides. Consequently, they believe that there were both Serb and Muslim prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this position imply that the commission may know something about the executions?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you present to the Chamber the text that is in this box.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the mentioned stages, the backbone of the Muslims who would be released would be -- or, rather, the basis of the composition of the Muslims who would be released would be one-third the Muslim soldiers taken prisoner in the Sarajevo battle-field in general, and the rest would be the remaining Muslims captured in the activities of the liberation of Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does it passage tell you, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It indicates that there are captured members of the BH Army who participated in the combat around Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give us the date that is present in the stamp below?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 13 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the text above in the headline says the 12th of August; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does the commission count on these prisoners from Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the text, yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3868, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we go back to page 1 to see who this was copied to.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the commissions for the exchange of war prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, we're interested in those who this was copied to for their information.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's just disappeared from the screen. Can you enlarge it a bit. For information Dr. Radovan Karadzic, President of Republika Srpska. Dr. Momcilo Krajisnik, president of the Assembly of Republika Srpska. Dr. Nikola Koljevic, deputy president of Republika Srpska. The Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Mr. Sava Srbac, government secretary of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What conclusions can you draw? What sort of information would all these people who this is being copied to get including the president of the republic? Would they get alerted to the fact that there was something irregular in the matter?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D25246. Has this document been admitted? My apologies. 1D25250, please. I apologise. What we have right now is -- is what I'm looking for. Can we keep this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please see this for yourself, who is writing this to whom.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the State Commission writing to the Main Staff, and the commission for exchanges of east Bosnia and Drina Corps and the subject is delivery of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you paraphrase this. On the 14th of August they are --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seeking information about the number of prisoners within the AORs of east Bosnia and Drina Corps. Their release would fully be based on the previously agreed principles in order of capture of larger groups of soldiers of the Army of Republika Srpska, Vijenac, Lisaca, Majevica, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does this document tell you? What is this State Commission counting on?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that there are prisoners on both sides that can be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3869, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D25250 now. And the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, can you look at that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very small print, and there's a lot of text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us collectively who this is being sent to and to whom for information?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again it's the State Commission sending it to the various commissions for exchanges of the various corps, and it is being copied to the same addressees that we read in the previous document except that Mr. Dusan Kozic is mentioned here, the prime minister of Republika Srpska who I don't think was copied to in that previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see here it says by Thursday the 12th of October?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received a complete reply to our official letter from the commissions for exchange of prisoners of war of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and Eastern Bosnia Corps. From the commission for the exchange of prisoners of war of the Hercegovina Corps we received a reply that was missing information on the prisoners of war held in prisons in the zone of responsibility of the Hercegovina Corps. We still have not received answers from the commissions for the exchange of prisoners of war of the Drina Corps and the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I am just urging you to read and spoke slowly and that goes for myself as well, though I'm rushing to use up the time. Can we have the next page. Can you read this bit in order to implement the entire --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to succeed in carrying out this entire -- I don't know what this reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Project.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And knock the trump card from the hands of the opposing side. I suppose it reads related here to the question of the missing. It is necessary to secure quality information and something is erased here. I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read the last passage, still within the box.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the global, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the global interest of Republika Srpska, ensure that ICRC representatives can conduct their mission in terms of visiting prisons and registering prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, can you look at the bottom and the date. It reads 12 October.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 12 October 1995, signed by the president of the State Commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, does anything in here indicate that in mid-October the state authorities have their suspicions about the fact that there are no prisoners from Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification pending full translation, but before we do that, yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, my intervention isn't related to this document, it's one that we addressed a few minutes ago, the 12 August document, which was personally sent to Mr. Karadzic. That's actually already admitted into evidence, and the Prosecution's translation, I think, is substantively different at that paragraph that was highlighted and shown to the witness. That's P4975. The Defence translation says: Other Muslims captured during the liberation of Srebrenica and Zepa would make up the required numbers. The Prosecution's translation says: The required number of Muslims would be completed by the remaining Muslims captured during the activities of liberation of Srebrenica and Zepa. I think the implication of remaining Muslims is -- is quite different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But this is the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It's the same document, just different translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If we're dealing with the same document, there's no point of admitting it separately and if there is a translation issue, then there's a step for the Defence to take. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think we -- we don't have to admit the Defence document, but if you can order that the translation be looked at for revision that would be the simplest thing since there are two competing translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's for the Defence to file a request if upon examination of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Also, Mr. President, I'll leave it in your hands, but if the redirect of the witness is intended to show that there's nothing irregular going on here, there's nothing that would put anyone on notice, then perhaps the general should be redirected to this document again with a different translation and asked again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or if you'd like to further cross-examination -- recross-examination for this, the Chamber is minded to allow you to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave. The witness was presented with the original. The translation is something that matters for the Defence and the Prosecution, but it makes no difference for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, is the treatment of prisoners of war regulated by anything?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. We didn't receive a number for the last document, MFI, pending a full translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But let us find out whether that was identical to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not this one. It was the previous one, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 1D -- 1D25245. Yes. I was confused. Shall we assign that number for this one pending full -- mark it for identification pending full translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D25250 will be MFI'd 3869.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think 3868 was the one that was the duplicate, so then this should be 3868 if I'm following correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, did you hear the question? Is the treatment of prisoners of war regulated by anything or is it left to the discretion of those who capture individuals?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's regulated by the Geneva Conventions as well as the operational instructions that the Main Staff issued to its subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D42041. Can it be enlarged, please. We have the translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, can you just identify it? It's the 20th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the instructions that the East Bosnia Corps command sent to its subordinate units as to how to proceed in the event of arrest, capture, and transfer of enemy prisoners of war and other captives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does the preamble state that there were deficiencies in the practice?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From the point of capture to the point of the transfer to Batkovic; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please read this to yourself and then tell us what you think about the preamble.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened was that they were being taken to where they were not supposed to be taken, to the town command where they were being interrogated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat when he said that somebody could not interrogate soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first thing. They are alerting to the fact that the most frequent mistakes made were the fact that soldiers would take prisoners of war to the front lines, take them to the town command post and interrogate them, whereas they were not authorised for interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, the sentence you started: The majority.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of captured enemy soldiers get to be exchanged pretty soon and it is certain that they submit reports to their intelligence and security organs upon their return. Thus they are in the position to provide significant information about our forces, the level of the front lines' reinforcement, the manpower along the front line, equipment on the front line. Effects of destruction in the area, the mood among the fighters, and the population, the distribution of command posts, forward command posts, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that in line 8 interpretation is not good. They are exchanged soon thereafter, so happened to be exchanged. So it so happens that they are exchanged quite soon. Is that the sense of it, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For planning purpose, I'm asking. How much longer would you need to complete your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between 20 minutes and half hour after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you not just finish in just 15 minutes? Then we'll have a break. But the Chamber is minded to have a somewhat long break for an hour today and resume at 1.30. I take it there should be no problem with us finishing at 3.00 today. We resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, please take a look at the first paragraph. I hope you've had a look at all of them. Is this customary to have things taken from POWs, things that could make it possible for them to harm themselves or escape or something? Is there anything in this instruction that is not allowed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in Serbian. In paragraph 4 it is also prescribed how members of the VRS are arrested, what the procedure is for them, for volunteers, foreigners. Is there anything that is unusual here?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see anything unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Beforehand, you saw that most POWs were exchanged quickly. Can you tell us now in view of everything you saw earlier on and today, in view of the way in which state authorities function, those that are in charge of POWs, in all these documents and all these reports was there anything that would alarm the president of the republic in order to spur him to deal with that or interfere?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything that would call for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3870, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, during the cross-examination it was suggested to you that the conclusions concerning my participation in command are not exactly based on facts, so now I'd like to show you a few intercepts, 1D5838, please, or 65 ter 30883. Do you remember the crisis in the beginning of August 1993 in our relations and in our relations with UNPROFOR? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a crisis in Banja Luka, but that was September 1993. And in August I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Please take a look at this. Do you remember the crisis with Igman and Bjelasnica?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1993, in July and August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: K is Karadzic and they assume that there is Milovanovic, too, and in line 2 I say: Listen, we have a fallout here between the UN and Mladic. And I say it's huge embarrassment and he says regardless of what politicians decide, he will not withdraw -- can you read this to yourself?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Huge embarrassment. It's a disaster, he says. Regardless of what the politicians decide --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, can you read it to yourself. Down here it says: But, man, he has to say. He mustn't resist the political sides because it's playing into their hands. And further down it says that he's giving them proof that he has cut himself off from politics and he does what he wants. How does this fit into what you know on the basis of your studying of our documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This fully fits into what I wrote and said. He considered himself the operative Supreme Commander of the military, and he thought that it was the political echelons that bothered him in that respect.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the last sentence of your answer. What was it, Mr. Radinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that he saw himself as the operative commander of the army and that in the operative command it was the political echelons that bothered him and that was a source of misunderstanding, and that is how he understood that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3871, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, during the proofing, the preparations, you said that the situation was absurd, that both the military and the political people were right and there was a clash, and you said that it's in the nature of the military to strive to be victorious and the politics didn't want that. Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the classical discrepancy between politics and the military. Every military wages war to subjugate the other side and to win. However, it is the political echelon that has to decide what should be done and that things should be verified through talks either at the beginning or during or at the end. That which is achieved through military victories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you come to the conclusions -- conclusion that politics did not want victory and that therefore they differed from the military in that respect?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several indicators. The entire strategic concept was defensive. The grouping of forces is defensive. And the deployment in the area of responsibility meant statistical warfare and forces need to be manoeuvred in order to win a war, grouped. And all of that is rendered impossible by this strategy. In public speech at sessions of the Assembly and on other occasions I came across your views and those of your associates pointing out that we are not waging war to win over the -- to be victorious over Muslims but to have Republika Srpska for us. When I say "you," I mean you and your associates. I remember what Mr. Buha said at a session in 1995 when he reprimanded some generals who held something against you; namely, that Tuzla was not taken and Bihac and some other cities. And he said then, We did not go out in a war to conquer. It's a defensive war. And there was no need for us to do that. We don't want that belongs to others. That is what Buha said at one of the sessions. I think it was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off. We can barely hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 31687 is the 65 ter number I'd like us to see now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could it please be enlarged. I'm talking to General Tomanic here and I'm probably speaking from Geneva. I don't know whether he was a colonel or a general then, 1993.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably during the operation of Lukavac 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now they are interpreting and sometimes quoting. They say that I'm asking why our forces returned to Igman and then around the middle it says Karadzic repeats that it is pure idiocy. And then there is some swearing, that I'm going to dismiss certain people, execute them, and so on, and then there's the sentence where it says Karadzic went wild and said, Well, man, it's clear to me, the army is lying to me. They've been lying to me all the time. The reports I receive are never accurate. Neither Mladic nor anybody else can be a pompous fool, and so on. I'm saying all of this to a man from the Main Staff; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How does that fit into what you established as you studied documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly as I stated. You reacted whenever the army overstepped the boundaries that were established by the strategy that you and your associates laid down. As far as I can remember this particular case, this was about the Geneva negotiations for solving the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina when Mr. Izetbegovic threatened to walk out of the negotiations if it is not abandoned, you order this to be done, there was lots of resistance, but it was eventually accepted. It was handed over to UNPROFOR and later on they handed it over to the Muslims. And in 1994 this resulted with the loss of life of female nurses at this particular location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, did you have any observation regarding the words of mine when I said that I'm not believing the reports?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was your impression that you were not receiving accurate information in your reports and obviously you didn't. If that had been the case you would have known what the situation with the prisoners of Srebrenica was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit MFI D3872, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, you also mentioned my attitude towards humanitarian issues and the role of the army in that respect. I'd like to show you a document, 1D9577.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D9577. Could you please look --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It disappeared from the screen. Oh, now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Negative consequences of the decision of the Main Staff to impose a ban on the movement of international organisations. Can we have the next page, please. This is an aide-memoire by Mr. Kalinic, and this is what it says here, the penultimate paragraph: Absolutely stop the Main Staff of the VRS who doesn't have either the mandate or personnel for humanitarian issues from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can we please have the previous page in order to be able to finish the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Can you go back to the previous page. So the interpreters were not able to interpret your question in full because we moved to the next page. So take a look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, can you please look at the penultimate paragraph where the Ministry of Health is request the Main Staff to act as an arbiter in moral questions and humanitarian issues because they don't have appropriate mandate and personnel. What is your opinion about this?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree, because the Main Staff cannot act as an arbiter in political and humanitarian issues because it doesn't have the necessary personnel and resources. They should stick to military and security domain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you manage to find in the document any reasons why the Ministry of Health intervened in this manner and how this evolved? Were there any disagreements?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were disagreements. They were more restrictive than the politicians when it came to the movement and operations of international organisations, and that occasioned the violation of international norms and sometimes in these convoys there were weapons, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Radinovic, the interpreters couldn't hear the last part of your answer. Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The essence of my answer was that there were reasons for disagreements, particularly where -- when it concerned the movement of humanitarian convoys, international mediators, the ICRC, and the army was much more restrictive in that respect than the politicians. Truth to say, they had good reasons for that because there occurred violations of the rules governing humanitarian aid supply because the convoys sometimes carried weapons and other military equipment which is otherwise not permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have the last page. In post scriptum it's -- Kalinic says to amend the order of the president of the republic by adding the WHO, the World Health Organisation, UNICEF, and UNHCR, and the date is the 2nd of October, 1994. How does this fit with your conclusions regarding the position of the civilian authorities concerning humanitarian issues?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I concluded that the entire system of humanitarian aid and the system of international organisations and their organs was under the umbrella of state organs. The army was supposed to just check them at the check-points but they did not have the mandate either to stop them or to suspend them altogether.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3873, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution devoted quite a lot of time to your assertions concerning the issue whether the orders were carried out or not. Can we please have 65 ter 11423. This is dated the 14th of December, 1994. It is addressed to General Mladic and Colonel Tomanic, the commander of the 2nd Corps. Please read it to yourself.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this document from earlier on. The general here mobilised the president of the Executive Committee of Grahovo municipality, but you are just to be suspended and to be reverted to the previous situation, but your general order was that these things should not be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, was I right? If he puts the president of the -- president of the municipal government and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please finish the question and could the witness please wait before starting the answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It only takes more time. Please speak slow and put a pause. The interpreters find it difficult to follow, impossible. Could you repeat your question first, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, the act of mobilising the president of the municipal government and appointing him the assistant for morale, what effects would have it have on the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have adverse effects. The government would be without leadership, and it will have serious consequences.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3874, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have now 65 ter 111109.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 11109.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, we're not doing this in sequence. Although we're following the years, we are now in the year 1995. We started from 1992. Please read this document to yourself. It seems that the -- some of the deputies are asking a question.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A seminar was held and it had been organised by a General Gvero and the deputies wanted you to tell them what this was about and what was discussed there. You say that you knew nothing about that and you're asking for information about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How does this fit with your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This only confirms that there was parallel channels.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3875, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D9563.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is from March 1995, the 15th of March. Please tell the Chamber what this relates to since there's no translation.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This relates to an order of the chairman of the State Committee for Co-operation with the UN, Mr. Koljevic, defining the obligations to allow unhindered passage of the UNHCR. Since this order was not carried out, you ordered it to be executed immediately and to state the reasons for not having carried it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who this was sent to?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was sent to the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska to General Mladic personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: By looking at this order, would you say that this was an isolated document, and how were these matters treated between me and the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not the only order of this sort. There were quite a few of them. I see many such -- I have seen many such documents, and this indicates also that there were disagreements within the chain of command from the Supreme Commander down to the Main Staff and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3876.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 13559.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read this document to yourself and then tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document sent by you to the commander of the Drina Corps, so the command of the Drina Corps and to the Main Staff for information. This pertains to an incident involving the driver of the brigade, Mr. Djuricic [phoen]. When he came to the check-point he spoke offensively about these people and particularly about yourself, and you are asking this to be investigated, that a statement be taken, and that a written report be submitted to you by the 23rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, can you tell us after having studied the documents that you had available, how did it happen that the commander's driver demonstrates this kind of attitude towards the president and --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this fits the picture of the entire system and the way you were treated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3877, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I have 1D9580.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We don't have a translation. General, can you tell us who I'm sending this to?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You sent it to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, to the sector or department for intelligence and security affairs, General Tolimir, 18 May 1995 is the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And here the Ministry of Health, Labour, and Social Welfare, whose minister is the president or the chairman of the commission for co-operation with international health organisations is complaining about the fact that he did not receive any response from the Main Staff to his letter about the freedom of movement. Can you tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Representatives of the international health organisation protested with this gentleman about the fact that the -- their work was being made impossible. So he approached Kalinic and they in turn are -- you are now in turn addressing the Main Staff about this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how does this reflect on your positions?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reflects my position about the relations between the army and the political structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3878, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at 15680, a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this decision of mine, and was it implemented? Look at item 1.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you present item 1 and its legality and whether it's justified?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hereby you decided that the -- you should rename the Main Staff of the VRS into the General Staff of the VRS. In time of imminent threat of war or in a state of war it would become the staff of the Supreme Command, and in keeping with the constitution and law, the staff would be immediately directed and commanded by the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your opinion about this item 1 is?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what I talked about when I talked about the positioning of the Main Staff within the military hierarchy. It should have been this from the beginning, what you were asking for, that it should be the General Staff that should deal with the use of army in peacetime, and of course in times of war it should become the staff of the Supreme Command and deal with the same issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What would in that case be the role of the Supreme Commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Supreme Commander would also be the operational army commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this order of mine implemented?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your order was not implemented because of the huge pressure that was brought to bear upon it by the public at large, official dignitaries and even the Serbian patriarch was calling upon you to desist from this idea and the entire generalship made this impossible or opposed this idea of yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3879, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say that the entire generalship did what was in fact insubordination, refuse to obey this?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, they said that they would not be executing anybody's orders other than the order of the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 13643, a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see this decree that I issued and is it in line with the previous document, and was it implemented, I mean this decree?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the president's decree appointing General Mladic as special advisor to the Supreme Commander, and it was not implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because General Mladic refused to implement it. Not just him but the entire generalship refused to have their structure transformed into the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3880, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 5906.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document dated the 5th of August, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the meeting in question here that I am denying the right of General Mladic to be engaged in this?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meeting is in response to your decision to rename the Main Staff and appoint Mladic as your special advisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what was the result of this meeting of theirs?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a result of the meeting, the parliament, as well as all the other important institutions in Republika Srpska, were publicly addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Addressed by whom and on what issue?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By generals, and the subject matter was -- or, rather, at the end of this press release it said that they would not be obeying anyone's orders other than the orders coming from the individual who is authorised for that, and that's General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3881, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 6559. We have this in English only so I'll read it out so that you get correct interpretation. First paragraph, 5 August: [In English] "General Ratko Mladic has refused to accept the post of special advisor and co-ordinator of the joint defence of the Serb republic and Republic of Serb Krajina to which he was appointed last night by Serb republic president, Radovan Karadzic. [Interpretation] And the last paragraph reads quoting Mladic: [In English] "'Therefore I shall remain at the post of commander of the main headquarters of the Serb republic army as long as our fighters and people support me, and until I am dismissed in accordance with the constitution and current laws on the army and defence,' Mladic said." [Interpretation] How does this fit into your findings?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- it fully confirms what I was saying right from the start, that the appointment of the commander of the Main Staff introduced a duality of authority in the army, and single authority was replaced by dual authority in the chain of command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Based on your research did I have actual operative control over our army, especially in the months of July and August 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D3882, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 15596. Apparently translation isn't completed yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Pay attention to this. It's 1st of September, 1995. Have you seen this document? And does it relate to the arrest of the parliamentarians who arrived in Pale with my consent?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this document during proofing. You were addressing the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, specifically to be delivered to the assistant commander for security and intelligence, General Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will read the penultimate paragraph. I quote: The European observers who we invited to come enjoy a privileged status of diplomats and parliamentarians. You should recall the fact that the Austro-Hungarian empire released Duke Putnik who was in their territory at the time when a state of war was declared. Do you recall that the Austro-Hungarian Empire did allow the first in command of the Serbian Army to return to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 2. What is my order here, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your order is that right after the formalities are dealt with and information is gathered, as well as clarification obtained from the RDB leaders, representatives of EU should be released and escorted to the border with the FRY and that they should be escorted by RDB organs in the same vehicle so that they could travel to Podgorica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Knowing all the various businesses that I had to attend to, was this something that I really needed to do?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly this isn't something that you needed to have on your hands as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you this be MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3883, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more document. Can we have 65 ter 14327.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, the date is 2nd October 1995. Can you tell Their Honours what does the preamble say, that something was done contrary to my orders, and what is my order?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You say here that pursuant to the order of the commander of the 2nd Corps dated the 28th of September, certain issues were ordered and regulated in contravention of your order, and you state what the order number is, and you are asking that the order of that command be made null and void forthwith and that your order should be implied instead, which relates to this issue, and you also demand that you be reported to about the execution of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it seems that we do have a translation after all. So after --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the transcript from the point where it reads "You say..., " it should be the witness's answer. Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3884, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, you were asked about your assessment of the degree to which Sarajevo was militarised.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D1923.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not think that I spoke about -- or discussed with the General the degree in which Sarajevo was militarised, or are you relating -- or is Mr. Karadzic relating to the military targets in town? If that question is meant, then it's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, precisely. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, can you tell us what is this map? Are you familiar with it, and if so, what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map depicts the location and types of military targets that were present in the urban core of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who drafted the map?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, I drew it. It appears to look like what I drew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you include this map in a publication of yours?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I included it in my book on Sarajevo. I did the same for my testimony in the case against General Galic. However, for reasons unknown to me, the Chamber refused to admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this map complete, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
